notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 11/22/2023
Patient: Casandra Crona, 69-year-old female

Study Summary:
Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 11/22/2023. The study evaluated sleep architecture, respiratory events, and oxygen saturation.

Findings:
Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 19.7 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 6% of all events. Sleep stages were adequately represented with normal distribution.

Oxygen saturation remained within acceptable limits with occasional desaturations corresponding to respiratory events.

Conclusion:
The polysomnography indicates moderate sleep-disordered breathing with a predominance of obstructive events. Central and mixed apneas are a minor component of the total events.

Recommendations:
Consider evaluation for treatment options including positive airway pressure therapy based on clinical correlation and symptomatology.

Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 08/13/2026
Patient: Casandra Crona, 72-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of obstructive sleep apnea with CPAP therapy.

History:
Ms. Crona has been using CPAP therapy for obstructive sleep apnea. Despite consistent nightly use, she continues to experience symptoms suggestive of inadequate control.

Physical Examination:
BMI 25.4 kg/m2.
No other significant findings noted.

Assessment:
CPAP failure: residual AHI 28.9 events/hour on CPAP at 10 cmH2O despite consistent nightly use.

Plan:
1. Consider alternative treatment options including advanced PAP modalities or adjunctive therapies.
2. Repeat sleep study to evaluate current sleep parameters and effectiveness of therapy.
3. Patient education on adherence and troubleshooting CPAP device.
4. Follow-up appointment in 4 weeks to reassess symptoms and treatment efficacy.

Summary:
Ms. Crona demonstrates CPAP failure with significant residual apnea events despite adherence. Further evaluation and management adjustments are warranted to improve her sleep quality and overall health.
